text:
Philip Broberg is the fastest skater we have data for (100th percentile in top speed), and this season the Blues have handed him the keys: 26 minutes a night over his last ten games, and a spot on the ice for 54% of their power-play time, up from 28% last season. He's answered with 7 goals and 18 points in 24 games, including a three-point night against New Jersey and goals in three of his last four as St. Louis won six of seven.

That's a real breakout in role. The scoring rate is not all real. He's shooting 14% against a likely 6 to 10%, and St. Louis has scored 12.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the biggest cushion in this group of players. At 5v5 the Blues take 47% of the expected goals with him out there, five points worse than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among defensemen last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him 95th percentile for slot chances, so the talent isn't in doubt. Expect the points to settle nearer 1.3 per 60 than the 1.8 he's at now.
